facts.source: Audiophile Style, thread "HQPlayer settings for specific DACs", the author's replies : « It is one of the dual-DAC designs, similar to T+A, where the PCM side is based on COTS DAC chip (AD1955) and separate DSD implementation »
facts.chip: A dual-converter design: a commercial AD1955 on the PCM side and a separate discrete implementation for DSD, which is why its family is the discrete DSD architecture rather than a chip vendor.

notes._optical_matters: This is the record that proves the optical default right. Six makers checked on 2026-11-20 put their optical input at 192 kHz, which was an argument for raising the catalogue's conservative 96 kHz assumption. Bricasti's datasheet says 44.1 to 96 kHz. One counter-example in seven is exactly the case the default exists for, and its failure mode is a device that does not lock and a zone that plays nothing - not a rate step nobody notices.
